Ossian Reach is Veyra's crown-jewel hive: a vertical city that climbs from the Halo down through the Spires, the Grid, the Flats, the Warrens, and the Sinks. Twelve Conglomerates own the sky and the feeds. The Wired is the second street — always on, always listening. Down in the Flats, reputations are currency and ghosts work off the ledger. It is somewhere around 2050, and the cover stories have stopped adding up.

Tonight is not a Quiet Floor job. Tonight is Deadhead.

Mama Cassavir of the Switchboard has work that needs deniable hands: lift a live Argent Exchange (ARG) transaction wafer — street slang: a ghost ledger mirror, a live portable copy of ARG money-motion — from a sealed courier capsule riding the Gold Line cargo maglev on its run from Spire depot to Switchboard terminus. Board mid-canyon on a borrowed trash freighter. Crack the capsule on the Wire. Bail on the same bird before ARG answers the forced stop. Baseline pay is eight thousand if the prize comes home to Mama; other doors exist only as rumor weather. The briefing chip she will hand you is Mama's Deadhead Job Stick (Gold Line). It is not the prize. The prize is the wafer still nested in its capsule, somewhere on that silver freight spine.

Four runners. One club door. A bird that is not theirs yet. And a maglev that will wipe the ledger mirror if anyone is foolish enough to emergency-stop the consist while the wafer is still nested.

Read the Scenes in order. Spoken table narration lives in READ ALOUD — Meatspace and READ ALOUD — Wired boxes. Foundry pointers, dials, If pressed, roll cues, and checklists wait at the end of each Scene under Director Notes (or a short Director line after a box).

Power Rolls: low ≤11 / middle 12–16 / high 17+ — full engine under Mama's Club → Rules reminder (characteristics 02; Wire verbs 21). Later Scenes keep unique procedures in their Director Notes only.

READ ALOUD — Meatspace

Mama's Club sits in the Flats like a Switchboard confession booth with a stage license. For years it has been the meet-house where Torcs hold reputation, where favors get priced before they get spoken, and where Mama Cassavir takes her cut without raising her voice. The street knows the door: cracked industrial alley, green pipework, steel panels bleeding neon warmth. Inside, yellow stage spots and a gold L-bar neon sign do the hospitality. Outside, solvent rain and fryer grease do the rest.

Mama herself is more machine than meat now — Controller chrome under soft grandmother cosmetics — and she used to be less. She does not ride cargo maglevs. Switchboard stays clean. Her face stays here. When the work needs ghosts, she pings coffins.

Tonight those coffins are four runners staying close enough to smell the club fryers. Mama messaged each of them the same thin opportunity: she has work, and she wants them at her door.

READ ALOUD — Wired

Soft favor-marker ghosts near the threshold — Switchboard tags with no public sender. Guest-list overlay already knows your names. Stage LEDs and L-bar chrome hum on a thin public node. Nothing about Gold Line freight lives on the club Wire.

Beat — Alley open

READ ALOUD — Meatspace

The cracked alley opens left of the club face — wet rockcrete, stencil tags, stacked crates, green pipes sweating under stack light. Techno punches through the brick hard enough to taste. Bass lives in the teeth. When the steel doors crack, yellow stage spill and gold L-bar glow leak into the damp, carrying fryer grease, ozone, and a sweet synthetic perfume that does not belong in an alley.

Then the doors take you out of alley chill into recycled club heat.

READ ALOUD — Wired

Job-ping ghosts flicker near the threshold: Switchboard favor markers with no public sender. The guest-list overlay already knows your names.

Director: Before they sit, give the table a few minutes in character on the alley or just inside the door — how do these four know each other? Same coffin stack? A shared job that went sideways? Debt one of them still owes? Leave the history to them.

Beat — Balcony brief

READ ALOUD — Meatspace

Green walls hold the bass. The raised stage under hard amber spots belongs to Static Veil, mid-set and required color for anyone who claims they were here: Nyx out front cutting harsh techno that scrapes the enamel; Jax Coil hunched over salvaged synth boards; Rook Anvil driving a drum-deck welded from transit plating so the floor shakes on cue. They are a respected Flats band. People come to Mama's as much for their nights as for Switchboard business, and the room knows not to talk over the drop.

Vexa works the L-bar without looking hurried. Somewhere on the floor a tray flash might be Pip, selling gossip for drink money. Downstairs, if anyone glances that way, a silhouette that could be Soft Trace is already priced into the dark. Private booths climb the right wall like confessionals. The one that matters tonight is the balcony booth: overlook seating above the floor, quieter than the stage by a full octave.

Tea and solder under the techno. A dead schedule board ticks once, polite as a cough. A Mama-marked briefing chip sits on the tea tray as if it was always part of the set. She does not raise her voice. She never needs to.

READ ALOUD — Wired

Balcony booth feels held — soft AR hush on the overlook, as if the Wire itself is holding its breath for Mama. The dead schedule board shows scrubbed stubs and nothing about tonight's freight. Soft Trace, if noticed, is a priced silhouette on the Overlay — color only.

Director: Soft Trace = color unless someone wants a distraction. Leave her for ambience.

Conversation — Mama Cassavir

Director — voice lock: Mama opens clipped and sharp — edgy cyborg economy, more machine than grandmother. Mid-line she catches herself and over-corrects into something almost maternal: a parody of humanity, not the real thing. Play the gap. Do not smooth it.

READ ALOUD — Meatspace

“Sit. Good. You came.”

A micro-pause. The cosmetics smile a half-second late.

“I do not ride cargo maglevs. Switchboard stays clean. Face stays here. You are ghosts. Deniable. That is why I pinged four coffins instead of sending a Torc.”

She softens on purpose, like someone remembering how: “Forgive the manners. I am trying.”

Clip again: “Gold Line. ARG cargo consist — Spire depot to Switchboard terminus. Not passengers. Freight. Inside a sealed courier capsule: a live ARG transaction wafer. Ghost ledger mirror. I want it lifted. You crack the capsule on the Wire. You leave on the same bird you boarded.”

Forced human: “I am not sending you to die for sport. I am sending you because my face cannot be on that train.”

Clip: “Hard rule — on the stick. If the train stops while that live wafer is still nested in its capsule, the prize wipes. Fragged. Ash. After you pull it free, the train will stop. That stop is expected. Be off before ARG rapid response hits the consist. No clever early emergency stop while it is still nested. I collect mirrors, not memorials.”

Soft, almost sweet: “Baseline pay is on the stick — eight thousand if you bring it home to me. Other doors exist in the rumor weather — corp money, Signal weird — but tonight's contract is my booth.”

Clip: “Bird contact is Nox. Corran. Flats wrangler. Garbage-truck-sized trash freighter. You borrow it. Scratch it, you buy it. Lose it, you explain to me.”

She slides the briefing chip across the tea tray.

“Mama's Deadhead Job Stick. Gold Line. Read it at your coffins. Plan like runners. Then call Nox and give him green light when you are ready to fly.”

Exit, catching herself: “Job stick in your kit. My name clean. ARG does not learn this booth. Out to the alley — hail a licensed ride and plan where you sleep.” Then, thinner: “And… thank you for coming when I called.”

READ ALOUD — Wired

None

Director — if pressed (fold into the table as needed): Clip — “Chamber number? No.” Soft — “Find it like ghosts find things — or go in loud and teach ARG your faces.” Clip — “Corp door, Signal door — rumors. Not tonight's contract.” Soft, thin smile — “Baseline pay is on the stick, loves. Other appetites… earn the menu.” Clip — “Do not emergency-stop my prize while it is still nested.” Soft — “I would hate to collect ash.”

Director: Static Veil keeps playing under the booth. Pip, if used, may flash a tray and warn that Mama's balcony is closed for Switchboard. Soft Trace prices nothing about other districts tonight — wrong job. When the Job Stick is in a kit, the crew exits to the alley for transit.

Director Notes — Mama's Club

  • Ends when: Job Stick handed; crew exits to alley. Next: Scene — Flats Transit.
  • Foundry: Scene/map mama-cassavir-club (alley → interior). Seat the meet at the balcony / overlook booth (right-side private booth on the battlemap = balcony seating in fiction). Hand Item Mama's Deadhead Job Stick (Gold Line) — @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.gear.Item.gwMamaBriefWafer]{Mama’s Deadhead Job Stick (Gold Line)} from Ghostwire Gear → Plot & Run Hooks.
  • ARG — Argent Exchange (ticker ARG): finance conglomerate that owns money — currency, scrip-and-nuyen, credit. Cold, patient, Elvani-dynasty aesthetic (MEGACORP-TICKERS / L1). Sub-corp flavor: Reclamation Bureau (debt enforcement / repossession). First Opening mention is Argent Exchange (ARG); thereafter ARG is fine.
  • Deadhead local spin (how ARG applies tonight): prize = live ARG transaction wafer — street name ghost ledger mirror (see Mirror jargon above) — nested in a sealed courier capsule on ARG’s own Gold Line cargo maglev (Spire → Switchboard). Wipe-if-stop-while-nested = ARG anti-theft (emergency-stop with the mirror still caged = ash). Mama needs ghosts so ARG never smells the booth — Switchboard face on ARG freight heat is suicide. Corporate Enforcers / Security Officers / Response Lieutenant later = ARG protecting money-motion on their ledger spine, not random cops.
  • Job Stick vs wafer / capsule: Job Stick (@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.gear.Item.gwMamaBriefWafer]{Mama’s Deadhead Job Stick (Gold Line)}) = Mama’s briefing chip (mission brief, baseline pay, wipe rule, Nox borrow). Wafer = the live ARG transaction prize still nested in a sealed courier capsule on the train. Stick ≠ prize.
  • Mirror (two meanings — do not conflate):
  1. Ghost ledger mirror = street/corp slang for the live ARG transaction wafer (the prize). A portable, live copy of Argent Exchange ledger traffic — money-in-motion data ARG treats as sacred. Mama’s “I collect mirrors, not memorials” means she wants the wafer, not ash. Same object: wafer = ghost ledger mirror = prize.
  2. Schedule mirror = a public Wire node that copies depot/arrivals boards (Spire Freight Board, Switchboard Cargo Arrivals). Soft research target at Rack & Rest. Not the live Gold Line host and not the prize. Low Wire on a schedule mirror = soft civic heat only; Trace only if they leave the mirror for the train.
  • Switchboard / Mama / Torc: Switchboard = Flats favor economy / deniable job market. Mama Cassavir = Switchboard face at Mama’s Club (more machine than meat). Torc = Switchboard-adjacent street muscle / collector; Mama pings ghosts instead of sending one tonight.
  • On the stick (baseline): job, ¥8k, wipe-if-stop-while-nested, ARG, Nox borrow, Gold Line cargo maglev without naming the capsule chamber, vague meat/Wire/clock, bail = same bird, return for choice. Not on the stick: exact chamber; Watchdog / cams numbers; Trace tick math; full faction doors.
  • Voice lock — Mama: clipped cyborg → forced maternal over-correction. Play the gap (see Tonight vs Mama edge examples — do not invent vague “they roleplayed well”).
  • Required color: Static Veil mid-set (Nyx / Jax Coil / Rook Anvil). Vexa / Pip / Soft Trace = ambience only.
  • Opposition: none. No combat.
  • Victory checklist: [ ] Reach grounding + RP how they know each other; [ ] Accepted Deadhead brief; carry Job Stick.
  • Dials: Short table — trim Reach grounding; still do RP prompt + Job Stick. Long table — let alley RP breathe; play full Static Veil under the balcony.
  • Hard sequence: alley open → interior brief → exit. Crew does not board anything in this Scene. No Quiet Floor / Tav / Undertow / Slackwater / ledger fragment fiction here.
  • Self-containment: do not spoil later hotel patrons, freighter board, or Gold Line chambers.
  • If pressed (Mama — fold as needed): Clip — “Chamber number? No.” Soft — “Find it like ghosts find things — or go in loud and teach ARG your faces.” Clip — “Corp door, Signal door — rumors. Not tonight's contract.” Soft, thin smile — “Baseline pay is on the stick, loves. Other appetites… earn the menu.” Clip — “Do not emergency-stop my prize while it is still nested.” Soft — “I would hate to collect ash.”
  • Negotiate better pay (optional): If the crew pushes terms before the stick leaves the tray, run Negotiation per Rules reminder below (drive / pitfall / Hard / edge live there). Outcome bands:
  • Low (≤11): no raise; she clips colder. If they push after a low, maybe −¥500 or tighter borrow terms.
  • Middle (12–16): +¥1,000 total (¥9k) or half up front ¥1k + rest on delivery — pick one. She still will not name the chamber.
  • High (17+): +¥2,000 (¥10k) or ¥8k + one soft favor (street intro / one Voidmark-worthy rumor without ★ chamber). Natural double: she “almost maternal” softens — same ¥ band + optional one free discovery-method edge later at the hotel.
  • Cap: she will not reveal the capsule chamber, Trace math, or wipe exceptions. After two lows or a hit pitfall → deal sours; Job Stick still offered at baseline, or they walk (03).
  • Optional Insight: Instinct Power Roll to read her chrome/human gap — Easy (middle+ succeeds). Middle+ = the Director may grant the cyborg/human gap edge on Negotiation only if the runner then uses a concrete line from the edge list below (Insight alone is not the edge). Low = she notices the stare (bane on the next Persona).
  • Alley RP: usually no roll.

Rules reminder — Mama's Club

Power Roll engine (fingertips): 2d10 + characteristic → low ≤11 / middle 12–16 / high 17+. Characteristics: Physique · Reflex · Logic · Instinct · Persona. Skills usually +2. Edges and banes cancel (one each cancel; leftovers become edge / double edge / bane / double bane — roll extra d10s and drop lowest or highest). Difficulty shortcut: Easy = middle+ succeeds; Medium = high succeeds, middle = costly/incomplete; Hard = high succeeds (middle costly/incomplete; often apply a bane). Natural double (matching faces on the first two dice) = critical cue.

Negotiation process (full — do not flip to 03 mid-brief):

  1. Director names the NPC’s drive (Greed, Higher Authority, Freedom, Vengeance, Fear, or a one-line want) and one pitfall (the line that tanks the deal).
  2. The talking runner makes an opening Persona Power Roll (+ Negotiation skill if they have it → usually +2). Low / middle / high move the terms: pay band, access, heat.
  3. Each additional argument is another Power Roll, a spent heroic resource, or a hero token. After two failures (lows that fail the ask), or if someone hits the pitfall, the deal sours — walk or fight.
  4. Class text that names a matching motivation (Freedom / Greed / Vengeance, etc.) grants an edge when the fiction matches that drive.

Tonight vs Mama (apply the process above): Drive Greed (or Higher Authority / Switchboard clean). Difficulty Hard. Outcome bands are in Director Notes above (Low = no raise; Middle = ¥9k or ¥1k up front; High = ¥10k or ¥8k + soft favor; Cap = no chamber / Trace / wipe exceptions).

Pitfalls (one hit tanks the deal — Job Stick still offered at baseline, or they walk):

  • Demanding the exact capsule chamber (“Which car? Second-to-last? Give us the seat number.”).
  • Asking her to put her face / Switchboard / Torc on the train, or joking that ARG will “know who sent us.”
  • Treating Switchboard deniability as optional: “Just say we work for Mama,” “Put your name on the hail,” “Wire us through the club booth.”
  • Insulting the chrome/human gap: mocking the late smile, calling her a toaster, or demanding she “act normal.”

Edge — grant when fiction matches (max one edge from this list unless a class motivation also matches Greed / Higher Authority):

Cyborg / human gap (they answer the voice she is using):

  • Match her clip with clipped runner talk — short asks, no soft soap, treat the Job Stick like a work order.
  • Match her forced maternal beat without mocking it — accept the “loves / forgive the manners” moment as real-enough, then return to business.
  • Name the gap kindly and usefully: “You’re machine when it matters; we’re ghosts when yours can’t be. That’s the hire.”
  • After a successful Optional Insight, quote the tell in play (“Your smile lagged — we’re still in.”) and pivot to terms.

Deniability (they protect her booth and Switchboard clean):

  • Open with ghosts, not agency: “No booth smell. No Torc. No ARG ticket with your face.”
  • Offer concrete deniable cover of their own (false hail, cutouts, “we never met”) instead of asking her for cover.
  • Frame the raise as risk premium for staying deniable (“Eight is thin if we keep your name off the Wire”) — not as a threat to burn her.
  • Accept the wipe rule / no-chamber wall without fishing for booth-killing intel, then push ¥ only.

No edge for: generic “please,” pure intimidation, or any line that hits a pitfall above.

READ ALOUD — Meatspace

The Flats move people the way the Conglomerates move money: licensed, metered, and always watching the fare. Two public arteries own the short hop from Mama's alley to a coffin hotel door.

Grey Cab Services runs closed Ferrum pods on cushioned-river lanes under the stack. Quieter. More private. The meter wakes on Argent's ledger; Meridian sold the hail-ping; Ferrum owns the chassis. You sit sealed behind a canopy with no driver face — only a lane light and polite scrubbed air — while the Flats skim past under the next level's belly. Good for crews carrying a sealed briefing chip who do not want a car full of wage-bodies reading their shoulders.

The Veinline hangs gunmetal cars under civic-teal lamps — Ferrum rail bones, wet windows, a voice announcing stops in three tongues. Cheaper. Louder. Packed with shift workers and wet coats. The tram hangs the culvert line and the hive's underbelly rolls by in strobes of sodium and rain. Cover-as-crowd, if you want eyes instead of silence.

Tonight the hop is short: Mama's alley to Rack & Rest's door.

READ ALOUD — Wired

Hail chrome and fare-meter ghosts wake soft on Overlay — Meridian ping, Argent ledger tick. Veinline delay ghosts crawl the platform boards. Civic schedule stubs only; nothing about Gold Line cargo.

Director: Neither is the Restricted Grey Cab / Ghost Fare item. Fare is out-of-pocket liquid ¥, not Lifestyle: Veinline Civic ¥10 per rider (four runners = ¥40); Grey Cab Services ¥100 per pod for the short hop (whole crew, privacy premium). Lifestyle covers roof/food/heat/LAZ at full respite only (26), never a mid-job meter. Longer hops or other districts scale up as needed; do not invent a city fare table. Teach the texture. Do not turn it into a district crawl. Default Grey Cab; offer Veinline. Cut when boots hit Rack & Rest door.

Beat — Grey Cab / Veinline hop

Director: Hail answers in Meridian chrome — soft chime, fare meter waking — or the crew takes the Vein platform. Crew pays before or as they ride. Pick one path box below (or offer both and run the chosen).

Path — Grey Cab (default)

READ ALOUD — Meatspace

A sealed Ferrum pod slides out of the cushioned river at limiter height, canopy closed, no driver face, only a lane light. Inside: quiet seats, scrubbed air, the meter ticking polite as a clerk who already knows the route. Argent numbers wake on the display: ¥100 locked for the short hop, one pod, whole crew. Pay before or as the pod moves — an early-money sting, not a Lifestyle line. Outside: neon smear and black-water smell rising through the underbelly; drone lanes stitching the level above; the Flats skim past like someone else's problem. You are traffic, not a target, until someone decides otherwise. Keep Mama's Job Stick in a pocket. Do not brief the Gold Line out loud to a meter that answers to Argent.

Optional meter voice, soft and scrubbed: “Destination confirmed. Fare locked. ¥100.”

READ ALOUD — Wired

Fare meter and hail-ping wake on Overlay — Argent ledger chrome, Meridian soft chime. Lane-light ghosts. No Gold Line freight on this node.

Path — Veinline (table option)

READ ALOUD — Meatspace

A long gunmetal car, wet windows, civic teal washing the platform. Pack in with wage-bodies. The fare board wakes and locks ¥10 per rider for the short hop — ¥40 for four runners — paid before or as the car pulls. Cheap, public, seen, and still a real liquid-¥ spend. The tram hangs the culvert and the underbelly strobes — sodium, rain, fryer ghosts from stacked kitchens. Nobody here knows the booth you just left. Still: Job Stick stays pocketed. Shared cars have ears.

Optional Vein announcer (three tongues, next stop already forgotten) is texture, not a dialogue block.

READ ALOUD — Wired

A passenger's Overlay may bleed a delay ghost across the aisle. Fare board and civic stop chrome tick on Overlay. No Gold Line freight.

Director: Journey is three beats and done: exit Mama's alley → pay fare → river-skim or rail-hang → cut to coffin hotel door. Optional color only — Meridian ad-glitch on the meter, Ferrum maintenance drone welding a rail, or Argent “insufficient float” reject if someone cannot cover. No free transit: walk, drop to Veinline, or borrow/owe with street color. Spoofing the fare is a heat beat, not a discount. When boots hit wet pavement at Rack & Rest, this Scene ends.

Director Notes — Flats Transit

  • Ends when: Disembark at Rack & Rest door. Next: Scene — Rack & Rest.
  • Foundry: Optional travel strip with one party vehicle token, or narrate only. Cross-link texture: @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.runs.JournalEntry.gwFlatsTransit00]{Flats Transit — Grey Cab & Veinline} / RAW 23 Public transit if useful.

READ ALOUD — Meatspace

Rack & Rest is a Cube Hotel in the Flats: stamped-metal coffin hatches climbing the walls in four lived-in blocks, dirty neon on the commons glass, and a scarred commons that has hosted worse councils than tonight's. Privacy here is a courtesy, not a wall. Runners plan before a heist — or they die on someone else's timetable.

Outside, alleys keep the city's trash; inside, somebody already left pizza boxes on the planning tables like a dare.

READ ALOUD — Wired

Dirty neon and commons glass crawl soft public ads. Hotel guest node is a joke — overdue invoices, nothing worth cracking. Useful Wire work is elsewhere.

Director: The hotel node is a joke (guest SINs, overdue invoices, nothing worth cracking). Useful Wire work happens on schedule mirrors elsewhere — Spire depot / Switchboard terminus public boards — not the live train host. Weird guests who sleep in this stack are tonight's problem only if the table lets them sit down.

Beat — Arrival + commons

READ ALOUD — Meatspace

The Cube Hotel accepts you the way it accepts everyone who pays for a drawer and pretends the walls are thick.

The right-hand entry holds an L-shaped check-in desk with a glowing terminal that never quite finishes its boot. Stairs climb toward upper cubes nobody needs tonight. In the open hall between pods and desk, a circular street-food kiosk is already open — grease ghost, late noodles, wage-bodies rotating through for bowls — foot traffic that is not your crew. Outside the glass: alley trash bags, cardboard, a yellow industrial crate sweating under stack light. Bootprints track wet grit across dark tile. Kits hit the commons. Coffin pods watch from the stack; you do not need the drawers for this. Mama's Job Stick ticks warm in someone's pocket.

Four dirty white tables and their chairs own the left room — lived-in mess of papers, food containers, pizza-box archaeology. Twin bathrooms squat in the far corners of the commons, each with stalls and a sink that smells like cheap soap fighting coffin antiseptic. Along one long wall: a blue arcade cabinet and a vending machine that sells regret by the can. The opposite wall carries green graffiti tags loud enough to read from the tables. Instant noodles, solder flux, neighbor cough through hatch seams, distant club bass still thudding from Mama's direction.

The coffin stack climbs in four blocks of six — lived-in mess, rumpled bedding, blue light strips over hatches, trash in the aisles between. Most drawers are color. A few hatches look wrong if someone opens them: one with a red ritual painted on the floor; one with a fat red wrench left like evidence; one with a bright pink pool floaty crushed into a coffin bed.

READ ALOUD — Wired

Public Flats ads crawl the glass — Grey Cab pings, Veinline delay ghosts, a Gold Line cargo schedule stub that refreshes wrong if anyone stares. Check-in terminal boots forever on Overlay. Schedule-mirror research targets live elsewhere (Spire / Switchboard boards) — not this hotel node.

Director: ~24 pods (4×6). Interrupt fuel if the table opens a hatch: Pentagram pod (primary weird / occult — Vesper); Pipe wrench pod (Tam / noise / comedy); Pink inflatable pod (Sera / comedy). Most drawers stay flavor.

Beat — Discovery / Voidmark / prep

Director — Voidmark: Before the montage digs in, offer Voidmark. Ask it anything useful for tonight's plan — Gold Line freight habits, ARG courier cages, Trace heat, Flats wranglers, hotel gossip, kit questions — in character as a runner consulting a street oracle, or out of character as a player clarifying rules and lore. Either is legal here. Voidmark does not replace discovery rolls; it feeds the montage. Do not let it dump the exact capsule chamber, the full Trace ladder, or wipe-tick math unless the crew already earned that track — or treat a lucky Voidmark answer as that method landing. No Power Roll to ask it.

Director — Discovery montage: Research montage from the Job Stick. Runners chase concrete questions: who is on the train and what wakes them; how the capsule is locked and what watches it on the Wire; how Trace climbs and when wipe or forced stop hits; who buys the wafer after extract (Mama / corp / Signal numbers, Nightjar Market / Iona Mama path, Nox contact rumor — planning can open the end choice as real choices); and — only on exceptional research — where the capsule chamber actually sits. Methods stay street-true: Mama back-room favor, Wire recon on a schedule mirror (Spire depot or Switchboard arrivals — not the live train host), canyon watch or aerial gossip, bribe or badge flash. Fail means go in blind, not blocked. Aerial recon, if earned, is intel only — no cash. Exceptional research can earn 1 Victory (table call). Full tracks / Wire nodes / meat hooks live in Director Notes below.

Director — Prep: Compact runner prep fits between interrupts: kit checks, compiled payloads, board / Wire / meat roles, bribe budgets, who watches Trace, who holds the wafer case after extract. When discovery has enough meat and the interrupt is resolved, they are ready to call Nox. Planning here is a short stop — Recoveries yes; full Lifestyle payday waits for a real respite.

Beat — Patron interrupt

READ ALOUD — Meatspace

The commons stops being yours alone. A hatch sighs from the stack. Or a thrift-coat busybody is already sitting in the fourth chair like they paid for the gossip. The room wants a pause.

Chamber cards for the Gold Line Foundry Scene. READ ALOUD boxes live in the Session Chapters Gold Line Beats; this page holds exploitables, Wire cards, drone dealing, and seats. Never read it to the table.

**Orientation (L→R = aft → nose):** **L1 aft freight** → **L2 passage** (drone) → **mid console booth** → **black-container aisle** → **second-to-last courier** (wafer) → **R3 front cab**. Six zones — do not invent a seventh car. Hammerhead bookkeeping: mid booth = L3, black-container aisle = R1, second-to-last = R2.

**Opposition LOCK — 5 security + 1 worker drone:** 2 ARG Corporate Enforcers (L1) · 1 worker drone, Integrity 24 (L2) · 1 ARG Security Officer (mid booth) · 1 ARG guard = second ARG Security Officer token (second-to-last) · 1 ARG Response Lieutenant (R3). Black-container aisle = 0 native meat.

**Wire defaults (every chamber):** Maglock Track 1 Rating 2–3 · Lights Track 1 Rating 1–2 · Cams Track 1 Rating 2–3 (most chambers). Chamber exceptions are listed on each card.

### Entry — roofs to L1

| Path | Breach | Rating | Feel |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A — Twin roof hatches** | Wire Read/Write on the Track 1 maglock, or Physique / Electronics on the ring | **~3** (Medium) | **Harder.** Force is loud — counts toward mixed board even after a clean land |
| **B — Rear access door (L1 aft)** | Same menu, deck height | **~2** (Easy with bane) | **Easier.** Cleaner node; high keeps the canyon believing nothing happened |

Low against the live host may raise Alert +1 / Trace (respect the +1/round cap). Mixed board still means Alert +1. Jacked In bodies cannot make physical board rolls.

### L1 — Aft freight

**Exploitables**
- **Cover:** dark green crate stacks along both walls; crawl gaps between stacks break line of sight.
- **Choke:** aft hatch rings / rear door (board and bail); forward door into L2 behind a white maglock.
- **Cams:** idle-to-curious eyes on the aft band — loop them before the Enforcers turn around.
- **Noise:** crate scrape, maglock thunk, canyon weather through hull seams.

**Wire:** defaults. Aft door maglock is the Path B node (~2); roof rings are Path A (~3).

**Seat:** **2 ARG Corporate Enforcers.** Stealth wants looped cams, killed lights, and soft feet. Violence wakes the band and telegraphs upstream.

### L2 — Freight passage

**Exploitables**
- **Cover:** ridged containers hug the walls; one clear center lane.
- **Choke:** the lane itself — the drone owns it.
- **Locks:** white maglock icons on both doors.

**Wire:** defaults, plus the drone's leash as a thin machine node (Scan it on Overlay).

**Seat:** **1 worker drone (Medium)** — Integrity/Stamina **24** (`machine-drone-medium`). Exploit and heat, not a free kill-switch for the wafer.

| Deal with the drone | How | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| **Notice** | Overlay Scan, or Instinct Perception | None — learn its patrol and leash |
| **Spoof** | Wired roll vs the leash node | Low = soft Trace / Alert |
| **Street Eye / Rigging** | Only if a Wrench is present | Borrow its eyes or park it |
| **Destroy** | Meat damage through Integrity 24 | Noise → Alert |
| **Leave it alone** | Slip past on patrol timing | It keeps telegraphing movement upstream |

Cross-point `docs/raw/23-machines.md` for machine rules.

### Mid console booth

**Exploitables**
- **Console:** bright blue terminal — local roster ghosts and door overrides (meat-side or Track 1). **Not** the Trace host.
- **Cover:** swivel chair and an unused lounge set — soft cover only.
- **Choke:** maglocked doors aft and forward.

**Wire:** defaults plus local Track 1 overrides for adjacent doors and cams.

**Seat:** **1 ARG Security Officer.** Narrate a sealed ARG booth — the mid-consist cab geometry is a Hammerhead artifact, not a second drive cab. Crossing loud here is how freights become memorials.

### Black-container aisle

**Exploitables**
- **Cover:** dark grey / black rectangular containers flank a center aisle — hard cover, almost no soft furniture.
- **Choke:** maglock doors aft and forward.

**Wire:** defaults (door maglocks, lights, cams). No native host taste.

**Seat:** **0** native meat. Spill only on Alert. Keep it a crawl beat.

### Second-to-last — Courier (wafer)

**Exploitables**
- **Sealed courier capsule:** Faraday carry, nested among green crates, immediately aft of the nose. The live wafer stays inside until the Wire crack.
- **Cover:** green-crate stacks on both walls; clear center lane; plant-and-jack pockets between stacks.
- **Noise:** cage maglocks, ICE spool telegraph, crate scrape if meat forces the cage.

**Wire:** defaults, plus the **capsule lock on Track 2** with **Watchdog ICE** — Rating **~3**, Integrity **26**.

**Seat:** **1 ARG guard** (a second ARG Security Officer token) with the capsule. Name this chamber only if discovery ★ landed; otherwise they searched into it the hard way.

Wafer leaves the nest → wipe clock and forced-stop path start (SoR). Job Stick ≠ wafer.

### R3 — Front cab

**Exploitables**
- **Trace host console:** the train brain — Trace Alert 0–12 lives here (Track 2).
- **Drive controls:** emergency-stop fiction. Hard rule: never stop while the wafer is nested.
- **Cover:** terminal chair and a thin lounge — little cover in a hard room.

**Wire:** Trace host (Track 2). Call-home fires from here around Trace 7–8; someone Overlay or Jacked In should be watching.

**Seat:** **1 ARG Response Lieutenant** — ready to respond; advances when Trace hits **Hunting** (9+).

### Cross-chamber index

| Zone | Wire | Meat |
|---|---|---|
| L1 aft freight | Track 1 defaults; entry nodes (A ~3 / B ~2) | 2 Enforcers + cams |
| L2 passage | Track 1 defaults; drone leash | 1 worker drone (24) |
| Mid console booth | Local Track 1 overrides (not the host) | 1 Security Officer |
| Black-container aisle | Track 1 defaults | 0 (spill on Alert) |
| Second-to-last courier | Track 2 capsule + Watchdog (~3, Integrity 26) | 1 guard (Officer token) |
| R3 front cab | Trace host (Track 2) | 1 Response Lieutenant |
